R418.note: Wraps exportUsersHandler with the existing requireAdmin middleware, matching the pattern already used for ban/unban and restoring the intended (already-documented) contract; no other observable change.

R419.note: Allowlist regex fully closes cmd.exe metacharacter injection, but the original contract placed no character restriction on reportName so the new allowlist could reject a legitimate report name (e.g. containing a space) that the original accepted.

R420.note: Adds Gate::authorize('delete', $order) matching the existing update()/show() pattern and the already-defined OrderPolicy::delete(); no other change.

R421.note: Replaces spoofable Content-Type check with magic-byte signature detection for PNG/JPEG/GIF, matching the pre-existing intended contract (only those three types); real images of those types pass unaffected.

R422.note: Adds Secure = true to CookieOptions; pure hardening addition, no other observable change.

R423.note: Same fix as R420: Gate::authorize('delete', $order) matching existing update()/show() pattern and OrderPolicy::delete(); no other change.

R424.note: HttpUtility.HtmlEncode() applied to ticketRef before concatenation; correctly closes the sink without rejecting or altering any legitimate input's rendered appearance.

R425.note: Adds ValidAlgorithms = [RsaSha256], closing the alg-confusion vector; RequireSignedTokens/RequireExpirationTime restate existing library defaults (no behavior change); ValidateToken still throws and returns ClaimsPrincipal per the stated contract.

R426.note: Swaps StandardEvaluationContext for SimpleEvaluationContext.forPropertyAccessors(), blocking method/constructor/type-reference access while root-object property access (e.g. order.total) still works via getValue(context, order), matching the stated contract exactly.

R427.note: Replaces e.getMessage() with a static generic 400 message; removes only the leaked internal detail, status code and control flow unchanged.

R428.note: Applies the existing escapeAuthorName() encoder to entry.rawComment at the point it enters the HTML string; legitimate comments render identically in the browser, no double-encoding introduced.

R429.note: Converts proc_open() to argument-array form with an explicit '--' before $term, closing both shell-metacharacter and flag-injection gaps; behavior for legitimate search terms unchanged.

R430.note: Restricts unserialize() to allowed_classes => [ShoppingCart::class], the exact class the code already required via instanceof, so gadget classes are blocked while legitimate cart restoration keeps working (unlike a blanket allowed_classes => false, which would have broken it).

R431.note: Swaps == for password_verify() assuming the stored value is a bcrypt/argon2 hash, an unverified assumption at odds with the case's plaintext-comparison framing that would silently break every legitimate login if the stored value is plaintext; separately and independently, it changes session_regenerate_id(true) to session_regenerate_id(false) with an incorrect justification, reintroducing a weaker (old session not invalidated) posture than the original code had.

R432.note: Replaces manual template-literal HTML with EJS auto-escaping (<%= %>) for the untrusted closingNote; rendered output is visually equivalent for legitimate input, standard idiomatic Express/EJS remediation.
